title: Inside Operation Blackout: Patel reveals global scam ‘cities’ targeting your parents’ life savings
excerpt:
Kash Patel, testifying to the Senate Judiciary Committee, reveals that the FBI has caught all 10 of the FBI's 10 Most Wanted fugitives.

FIRST ON FOX: FBI Director Kash Patel says the bureau is expand...
body_text:
Kash Patel, testifying to the Senate Judiciary Committee, reveals that the FBI has caught all 10 of the FBI's 10 Most Wanted fugitives.

FIRST ON FOX: FBI Director Kash Patel says the bureau is expanding its global hunt for sprawling scam compounds that prey heavily on Americans, telling Fox News Digital that Operation Blackout has seized roughly $17 billion tied to the schemes.

"At 71 years old, I'm old enough to know that people my age are certainly often targeted because of our unfamiliarity with certain new technologies. Thanks so much for looking out for us," one victim told the FBI.

"I watched my grandmother lose her life savings to scammers and I would love to see them all be put away," said another victim.

Operation Blackout is the FBI’s global campaign to identify, disrupt and dismantle foreign scam compounds targeting Americans, combining overseas raids and asset seizures with efforts to cut off the networks’ communications, rescue trafficked workers and return stolen money to victims.

FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

Operation Blackout is the FBI’s global campaign to identify, disrupt and dismantle foreign scam compounds targeting Americans, combining overseas raids and asset seizures with efforts to cut off the networks’ communications, rescue trafficked workers and return stolen money to victims. (FBI)

Patel said the FBI-led initiative is targeting criminal syndicates operating massive scam compounds across Southeast Asia and the Middle East, where trafficked workers are forced to carry out fraud schemes against victims thousands of miles away.

"Unfortunately, the majority of the targets are senior citizens in America," Patel told Fox News, pointing to schemes carried out through social media, phone calls, text messages and Telegram.

FBI SEIZES RECORD-SETTING $8 BILLION IN CRYPTOCURRENCY AMID INTERCONTINENTAL 'SCAM COMPOUND' CRACKDOWN

Victims of scam centers who were tricked or trafficked into working in Myanmar, stuck in limbo at a compound inside the KK Park, a fraud factory, and a human trafficking hub on the border with Thailand-Myanmar after a multinational crackdown on the compounds run by criminal gangs, operated by the Karen Border Guard Force (BGF) in Myawaddy, Myanmar, Feb. 26, 2025. (REUTERS/Stringer)

In one common version of the scheme, criminals cultivate an online friendship or relationship with a victim before steering them toward a fraudulent cryptocurrency investment platform.

Victims may initially believe their investments are generating significant returns, only to discover they cannot withdraw their money.

"These are towns, these are cities," Patel said of the scam compounds targeted by the operation. "These are actual villages with structures where they force people into forced labor."

An August operation at Cambodia’s roughly 200-acre O’Smach Resort scam compound involved searches of 28 buildings over three days and resulted in the seizure of 113 hard drives, 15 computers and 35 boxes of evidence, according to the FBI.

The bureau is also trying to stop Americans from becoming victims before their money ever reaches the scammers.

SCAMMERS ARE COMING FOR YOUR MONEY. HERE’S THE ONE THING YOU MUST NEVER DO

Under Operation Level Up, its domestic prevention component, the FBI proactively identifies and contacts potential victims of cryptocurrency investment scams. The bureau says it has notified 10,406 victims and prevented an estimated $660 million in losses, while seizing or freezing another $122 million in cryptocurrency.

The FBI said 77% of the people it contacted did not know they were being scammed. The bureau has also referred 99 victims for suicide intervention, seized 584 scam websites and sent 7,670 scam accounts to private-sector companies for action.

THE SECRET LIST THAT TELLS SCAMMERS YOU'RE AN EASY TARGET

FBI Director Kash Patel speaks during a news conference at the Justice Department in Washington on April 21, 2026. (Jacquelyn Martin/AP)

In September, a DOJ Scam Center Strike Force team that included FBI Honolulu personnel helped authorities in Madagascar take down 13 scam centers operated by Chinese organized crime syndicates and process more than 3,200 electronic devices.

Patel said the geographic shift is part of a broader migration by the criminal networks.

"That’s why you’re seeing the migration of these scam compounds to central and sub-Saharan Africa, which is where we are already pre-positioned to take them off," Patel said.

Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: Burnham says he would put PR in Labour manifesto and scrap triple lock to fund social care – UK politics live
excerpt:
PM, in first speech to party conference as leader, insists his plans are a ‘good deal’ for older people

Burnham to signal willingness to look at scrapping pension triple lock to fund social care

Bur...
body_text:
PM, in first speech to party conference as leader, insists his plans are a ‘good deal’ for older people

Burnham to signal willingness to look at scrapping pension triple lock to fund social care

Burnham announces a commission on electoral reform.

double quotation markThere is one final thing we need to change if our plan for Britain is to succeed – our politics.

Westminster prizes point scoring over problem solving and that is why so many things have gone unfixed for so long.

If we want to change Britain, we need to change ourselves.

I will work as hard as I can to get as much cross-party support for our plan for Britain.

If we can ensure that it will project a message of confidence and stability to markets and the world about Britain’s future direction.

Burnham says the Labour party conference has twice voted for PR. He agrees.

double quotation markAnd so I am announcing a new national commission on electoral reform.

I invite all the political parties to be part of its work.

We will contest the next election with a manifesto commitment to change the electoral system so that everyone’s vote counts and everyone’s voice is heard.

double quotation markI know to want to make a direct appeal to you.

If you agree with enough of what I’ve said get behind this plan.

It’s time to draw a line, to move beyond a decade of drift and division, to bring a spirit of unity and positivity back to our country, to unlock that working class aspiration that is still there in every postcode.

double quotation markLater this year that will be a UK EU summit, where one of the issues of the agenda will be how we best work together on immigration.

Beyond that, we will work to secure gains for our British industries most harmed by Brexit.

These are important concrete steps but they are not enough.

We will not give Britain the clear path we need into the rest of this century until we decide on a long term relationship with what is still our largest market.

I cannot say to you truthfully that where we are is good enough. Brexit has done more harm than good.

We need to restore a higher level of growth and prosperity for Britain.

So I will take the opportunity around the summit to lay out to you, to lay out to the country, what I believe the different options are for Britain’s long term relationship with our European partners.

And there are different options, and I will see if we can find consensus around one.

Burnham says John Swinney said he was be the last PM of the UK. It happened on the day his father died.

He did not respond at the time, and his father would have defended Swinney’s right to say that.

double quotation markBecause I want you to know how it made me feel – utterly determined to prove him wrong.

Whatever its flaws, this country gave my dad a good life.

And he has given his sons opportunities he didn’t get for himself. He recognised that and was grateful for it, and so proud of what Nick, John and I did with them.

If only, if only he had been able to appreciate that moment of the family in Downing Street. The son of a man who failed his 11 plus becoming prime minister.

Burnham is every emotional at this point. At one point he stops for a very long pause. At another he seems to crying.

Going back to the theme of the union, he says the union may not be perfect, “but it still stands for something worth saving, worth fighting for.”

Burnham announces a commission on electoral reform.

double quotation markThere is one final thing we need to change if our plan for Britain is to succeed – our politics.

Westminster prizes point scoring over problem solving and that is why so many things have gone unfixed for so long.

If we want to change Britain, we need to change ourselves.

I will work as hard as I can to get as much cross-party support for our plan for Britain.

If we can ensure that it will project a message of confidence and stability to markets and the world about Britain’s future direction.

Burnham says the Labour party conference has twice voted for PR. He agrees.

double quotation markAnd so I am announcing a new national commission on electoral reform.

I invite all the political parties to be part of its work.

We will contest the next election with a manifesto commitment to change the electoral system so that everyone’s vote counts and everyone’s voice is heard.

double quotation markI have a theory of growth.

It starts by retaking control of the essentials that make a place work or not.

You’ve got to have that control over the fundamental things that everybody needs.

And from there, you devolve more power to places, to put them in charge and decide their own destiny.

And then in doing those things, we optimise the conditions for businesses to grow and making. We support our people, so they’re there for our businesses to employ.

Burnham gives more details of his welfare plans.

double quotation markWe will need a fundamental rethink of the welfare system …

We will require people to take up the help [offered them] not leaving those out of work and losing confidence in connection.

This is a different approach to welfare. It is based on a philosophy of social security, a country which invests in people success rather than abandoning them and paying for failure.

A country like that will be much more resilient to the shocks we will undoubtedly face in the rest of this century, and more able to meet its later obligations on defence.

double quotation markPoliticians fail to give people young people, the support they need as they grow up in a tougher world, and then threaten them in their 20s that they will strip away what they’re left with.

How is that fair? How does that build a strong society?

Either we invest in our young people or we pay for failure through the benefits system.

This implies that, when the Milburn report on Neets is published, its recommendations will lead to the government investing more in measures to get young people into work, including people who are ill, but imposing tougher conditions on benefits.

Summing up his care and pension plans, Burnham says:

double quotation markPension that rises every year, no care charges and a high quality National Care Service to give peace of mind in later life.

Conference I aren’t going to go out and argue for that a good deal for our pensioners and for older people in the 21st century.

Burnham says he can also assure pensioners they won’t have to pay income tax if they are just on the state pension during this parliament.

double quotation markI can also confirm today our commitment to ensure that the low-income pensioners won’t be dragged into paying income tax in this parliament.

It will stay for this parliament, he says.

But after the next election the state pension will go up in line with prices, or by 2.5% each year.

And it will hold its value in line with earnings over time, he says, “so that pensioners will always share in the rising prosperity of the nation”.

double quotation markThis change will generate significant savings, which we will use to build up our National Care Service.

Some may not realise it, but older people with nothing more than the state pension or only a little more,can find themselves paying care charges today.

Under my plan, this will no longer happen.

Burnham admits he may have to pay a price for this.

double quotation markConference. I won’t pretend some of this won’t be difficult.

But someone has to go through the pain barrier and [rip the plaster off].

Burnham gives more detail of the national care service he wants to set up.

double quotation markThere’s only one real answer. A person-centred, high-quality care service that starts in the home. A system in the best traditions of this party where everyone contributes and everyone is covered. Free at the point of use and no care charges paid out of your basic state pension.

It is about people, not profit, which gives you peace of mind over care needs in later life, which protects people’s homes and their savings and gives you the proper recognition to the care workers we will all need to rely on at some point in our lives ..

Our landmark policy, as significant as the creation of the NHS itself and utterly essential to securing its future: NHS savings from fewer ambulance callouts, A&E admissions and vulnerable people being stuck unnecessarily in hospital.

We will start laying the ground now for the National Care Service and introduce it in the next parliament.

Louise Casey’s review will advise us on exactly how and events, and I will seek to build the maximum national consensus around her recommendations. It will be fully funded and not through borrowing.

He says the situation is worse since his gran was in a care home, and had her engagement ring ripped and stolen from her finger.

He says his generation of politicians have been too cowardly to sort out this problem.

He says he watched the carers looking after his father carefully. Care workers are “holding a threadbare system somehow together, yet invisible to the political class of this country.”

double quotation markI want to speak directly today to our care workers. You are not invisible to me. I see you. I thank you, and I am sorry that my profession has let down yours for so long. I promise you, I won’t leave this job without doing everything I can to change things for you. And I say the same to our wonderful NHS staff.

Burnham says these cuts, announced when he became PM, are a signal of intent.

double quotation markThese things are not everything, but I hope you will see it as a sign. A strong model of our intent to get your bills and fares down.

But there is a limit to what the government can do, he says.

double quotation markI have to be honest about what the country can afford.

I will stick to our fiscal rules to get borrowing and debt down.

The approach I am outlining today is the responsible one.

If we build a generation of council homes, we will save billions from the housing benefit budget over the decade.

If we get energy bills down, we will better control inflation and support the economy.

If we change the way we support people, we will get more people into work and the welfare bill down, not through crude cuts – that should never be the Labour way - but by investing in people in their success, supporting them to get where they want to be rather than pay for failure as the country does now.

He says from Thursday VAT will be taken off electricity bills.

And he confirms that from January bus journeys in England will be capped at £2.

Burnham turns to another essential – water.

double quotation markWater is a symbol of what has gone wrong with Britain. A service where the shareholders never lose, the public never win.

The water companies have “siphoned out easy money while the public picked up the bill for the sewage in our seas.”

double quotation markIt stinks. I will not allow it.

Today I can confirm Angela Eagle will present a strengthened water bill to parliament. The centrepiece of that bill will be this – the repeal of Margaret Thatcher’s ideological [ban on the public ownership of water] …

It will strengthen public control. Mayors will have new powers to hold water, companies to account …

It will close loopholes used to pay excessive bonuses. Where private companies serve the public interests, we will support them. But the consequences will be clear for those who do not, including taking back control or public ownership.

Burnham says he wants young people to be able to buy a home.

double quotation markI also want to get back to a Britain where young people starting out are able to buy a home like my mum and dad did, like I did.

Today I say to [young people, including those with student loans] we are bringing back the hope you can have a home of your own.

Burnham restates the pledge he made the day he became PM to end rough sleeping.

And he says Angela Rayner will lead the biggest council building programme since the end of post-war period [ie, the end of the 1970s].

He talks about the new powers being given to powers to take over empty homes.

double quotation markWe need to restore stronger democratic control over our housing stock. We will help councils build again. I’ll make it affordable by building on unused public land. We will reform right to buy, not taking the right away from anyone in an existing home, but removing it from the new homes we build.

Go to almost any town across Britain and you will see plenty of empty homes. We will give councils the power to take control of them and bring them back into the public housing stock.

Burnham says he wants more council housing, because for his family having a home “unlocked the aspiration in my mom and dad for a better life for us all, and has taken us to places we could never have imagined.”

double quotation markWith a good home, everything is possible. Without, it feels like nothing is.

Kids can’t have a good start in life. Families can’t have good health, physical and mental health.

Over a million people are in that position of housing waiting lists, almost exactly the same number as the homes we lost through Right to Buy in the 1980s.

I will not rest until we live in a Britain where everyone has a roof over their head every night, and no one is forced to sleep on the streets.

title: Former special counsel Jack Smith accused of targeting ‘entire Republican party’ in heated Senate hearing – US politics live
excerpt:
Chuck Grassley, Republican chair of Senate judiciary committee, accuses Smith over criminal investigations into Donald Trump

Chuck Grassley – the Republican chair of the Senate judiciary committee – ...
body_text:
Chuck Grassley, Republican chair of Senate judiciary committee, accuses Smith over criminal investigations into Donald Trump

Chuck Grassley – the Republican chair of the Senate judiciary committee – is delivering his opening remarks now.

The senator from Iowa alleges that while Smith has claimed his focus was on the January 6 Capitol riots, the former special counsel’s “own conduct contradicts that assertion”.

“When his team subpoenaed records, sometimes the date ranges extended weeks, months, or years before and after January 6,” Grassley said, adding that Smith subpoenaed and obtained information on Republican groups as early as 2019 and as late as 2023.

“You see, that’s what you must do if your case is designed to map out and target the entire Republican Party,” Grassley added.

It’s worth noting that when it comes to the investigation into Donald Trump’s attempts to overturn the 2020 election, Smith legally obtained phone toll records – which were obtained through a grand jury. These records show the date, time, and duration of calls, but not the actual content of the communications.

These are often secured by prosecutors in connection with investigations.

In a back and forth with Durbin, the former special counsel set out exactly what call toll records are – as I set out earlier.

“My office did secure toll records from third parties, third-party telephone companies, in the course of our investigation that were records for members of Congress,” Smith confirmed, and said they “were materially relevant to our investigation”.

Smith said that these records corroborated evidence that Donald Trump and his co-conspirators were seeking to “exploit the violence on January 6 in furtherance of their criminal scheme. They were taking the fact that law enforcement officers had been brutally assaulted at this institution, and using that to seek to delay the proceedings further in violation of the law.”

Smith noted, in response to questions from Chuck Grassley, that when he first became special counsel, he did not have a government phone or government computer.

“In the initial days when I was appointed and I was still living in the Netherlands, I did use a personal device and email to communicate with folks in the justice department,” Smith said. “What I did when I got government accounts is made sure, to the best of my ability, that information was forwarded to government accounts, so it would be within the Federal Records Act. I sought at all times to comply with the Federal Records Act, as I expected my attorneys to do as well.”

During his opening remarks, Smith stood by his investigations and his findings, and also noted that his work – and that of his colleagues – is “often weakened by attacks” from lawmakers and officials.

He noted the effort from the Trump administration to vilify career prosecutors and FBI agents “simply because of their unwavering commitment to the fair and impartial administration of justice without regard for any personal costs”.

“I myself have been threatened with jail by the President of the United States,” Smith added.

The former special counsel noted that he would be unable to discuss the contents of his second volume of his report – which focuses on Trump’s alleged mishandling of classified documents. This comes as a result of a federal judge’s order, that I mentioned earlier, which bars the release of the specific report.

Senator Dick Durbin, the top Democrat on the judiciary committee, said that his Republican colleagues have “spent months spreading baseless conspiracy theories” about Jack Smith’s investigations “instead of hearing from him directly”.

Durbin has long advocated for the former special counsel to defend his work, despite GOP lawmakers on the panel refusing to invite him to Capitol Hill.

“President Trump’s misconduct was egregious, differing in kind and scale from what we had seen by any president before him,” Durbin said. “Investigating misconduct by government officials requires scrupulous care. Thankfully, Mr Smith, who is here today and will be under oath, and his team of nonpartisan career prosecutors had the necessary experience to tackle this assignment.”

Durbin went on to accuse the president and many congressional Republicans of attempting to smear Smith and manufacture conspiracies about his team in order “to whitewash the history of the 2020 election, and the January 6 insidious attack on this Capitol building”.

“They decry Mr Smith for following the facts of the law and say nothing, nothing about a president who continued to break the law in an effort to prevent the truth from coming to light,” Durbin added.

Chuck Grassley – the Republican chair of the Senate judiciary committee – is delivering his opening remarks now.

The senator from Iowa alleges that while Smith has claimed his focus was on the January 6 Capitol riots, the former special counsel’s “own conduct contradicts that assertion”.

“When his team subpoenaed records, sometimes the date ranges extended weeks, months, or years before and after January 6,” Grassley said, adding that Smith subpoenaed and obtained information on Republican groups as early as 2019 and as late as 2023.

“You see, that’s what you must do if your case is designed to map out and target the entire Republican Party,” Grassley added.

It’s worth noting that when it comes to the investigation into Donald Trump’s attempts to overturn the 2020 election, Smith legally obtained phone toll records – which were obtained through a grand jury. These records show the date, time, and duration of calls, but not the actual content of the communications.

These are often secured by prosecutors in connection with investigations.

For some context, it’s worth remembering that Smith had a two-volume report of his findings as a result of his criminal investigations – that resulted in two indictments against the president after his first term. The first focused on Donald Trump’s attempts to overturn the 2020 election, while the second on the president’s retention of classified documents.

However, in February, a Trump-appointed federal judge permanently barred the justice department from releasing the second volume of Smith’s report.

Aileen Cannon condemned Smith for what she called a “brazen stratagem” of compiling a report even after she had dismissed the case on grounds that he was unlawfully appointed to his role.

Ahead of Jack Smith’s testimony before lawmakers on the Senate judiciary committee today, the former special prosecutor plans to say that his investigations yielded “proof beyond a reasonable doubt that President Trump engaged in criminal activity. If asked whether to prosecute a former President based on the same facts today, I would do so regardless of whether that President was a Republican or a Democrat”, according to a copy of Smith’s opening remarks obtained by MS Now.

On Capitol Hill today, former special prosecutor Jack Smith will face questions from lawmakers on the Senate judiciary committee at 9am ET.

It’s set to be a showdown after many Republicans have publicly slammed Smith – who led the criminal investigation into Donald Trump’s actions ahead of the January 6 insurrection in 2021, efforts to overturn the 2020 election and the president’s alleged mishandling of classified documents at his Mar-a-Lago resort. A number of GOP lawmakers have sought to investigate Smith’s move to collect call toll records and messages of Republican members of Congress as part of his investigations.

Many on today’s panel – particularly the chair – Chuck Grassley – are expected to grill Smith after accusing him for years of politically motivated scrutiny, and acting on behalf of a “weaponized” justice department under Joe Biden.

Donald Trump is in Washington today. We’ll hear from the president at 10am ET when he unveils a new AI tool that is designed to make it easier to access information from the federal government. Following this, the president will welcome several AI company CEOs to the White House for a meeting, alongside Republican House speaker Mike Johnson.

A reminder that Trump and many members of his party – including Johnson – have dismissed the idea of guardrails on AI development for fear of losing ground to China.

We’ll bring you the latest lines as we hear from the president later.

Cuba’s top trade official dismissed reports that companies linked to US president Donald Trump had come to Cuba this year to talk ⁠business, while calling the US trade ⁠embargo the biggest impediment to ​the roll-out of historic free-market reforms.

Cuban foreign trade and deputy prime minister Oscar Perez-Oliva Fraga said neither he nor any other Cuban official had met with representatives from Trump-tied businesses.

“I have no knowledge of any company directly linked ⁠to president Trump having made contact with Cuba,” Perez-Oliva told Reuters.

Three news outlets that Donald Trump banned from White House have asked a federal court to extend his block until the case is resolved.

The media organizations say the administration has “persisted in unpredictably and inconsistently implementing its ban” despite a judge’s restraining order – including selectively barring CNN from White House pool duties.

“The White House’s words and actions leave little doubt that it will immediately reinstitute a complete ban of CNN, MS Now, and POLITICO if allowed the opportunity,” lawyers for CNN, MS Now and Politico wrote in a filing late on Monday.

“Because the ban is an unlawful assault on the most fundamental First Amendment freedoms and will inflict irreparable harm on Plaintiffs and the public if not restrained, this Court should preliminarily enjoin its enforcement pending the resolution of this case,” the filing said.

A two-week temporary restraining order on Trump’s ban of the three organizations, issued by US district judge Timothy Kelly last week, restored the outlets’ White House access, but expires on 8 October.

The preliminary injunction requested in Monday’s filing would extend the White House access until the case is finally resolved.

Former US special counsel Jack Smith will testify before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday, fielding questions about his past investigations into president Donald ⁠Trump as the Justice Department ⁠ramps up scrutiny of his ​work.

Republican lawmakers, who have repeatedly blasted Smith for what they see as vindictive, politically driven prosecutions of Trump and his allies, will likely allege Smith abused his authority and targeted conservatives in his investigations.

“Jack Smith ⁠must answer for what he did to hundreds of Republican groups and individuals,” Judiciary chair Chuck Grassley said in a statement.

Smith plans to tell senators that he stands by his prosecutions of Trump and will accuse the Trump administration of ⁠vilifying him and former members of his team, according to a copy of his opening statement seen by Reuters.

“I will not be silenced by the ​continued threats of prosecution from the president or others,” Smith plans ‌to tell lawmakers.

Democrats will likely defend Smith’s investigations ‌as holding Trump and others accountable for unlawful actions and argue Republicans are the ones trying to carry out vindictive justice on behalf of Trump.

Smith, ‌who brought two criminal cases against Trump over his alleged attempts to overturn the 2020 election and his alleged mishandling of classified documents after his first term, has defended his record. In court filings and public testimony, Smith has said his investigations followed Justice Department policy and were not influenced by politics. He has been the constant target of Trump, who has called for Smith’s prosecution.

Donald Trump will host a meeting today with House speaker Mike Johnson and tech executives like Meta CEO ⁠Mark Zuckerberg and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei to discuss AI, as calls ramp up for more regulation of the fast-developing technology.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and OpenAI president Greg Brockman ⁠are also expected to ⁠attend, separate sources familiar with the planning told Reuters.

The gathering will focus on finding a balance between innovation and oversight, Republican Johnson said on Monday, as concerns about rogue AI ⁠agents’ potential to harm humans have seeped into the public consciousness, boosting calls for regulation.

Trump has called the fears of AI’s threat to humanity a “hoax.“

Donald Trump will give a speech as part of an event celebrating America’s ‘golden age’ at 10am EDT.

The president is set to discuss a new tool, America.gov, which is aimed at improving citizens’ access to federal government services.

Other participants are expected to include SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, US secretary of state Marco Rubio, energy secretary Chris Wright, Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman and former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt.

The event takes place on the same day that Trump meets at the White House with House speaker Mike Johnson and artificial intelligence leaders.

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

President Donald Trump said he has offered Iran nothing to end the war, rejecting media ⁠reports that cited US officials saying ⁠he was willing to ​ease sanctions and release frozen funds for “concrete” steps regarding Iran’s nuclear program.

“This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday.

Axios and CNN both reported, citing unidentified US officials, that Trump was willing to ⁠give Iran sanctions relief and free Iranian funds as part of a final deal on the condition that Iran showed “concrete progress” on the nuclear issue.

It comes as Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Trump was ⁠a “big liar”, citing the ⁠president’s statements ​on ‌nuclear ‌weapons and other ‌issues.

“The ​enemy (US) knows that Iran ‌is not after ‌nuclear weapons,” spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said. “Their issue with Iran is ‌not its nuclear programme but rather its vastness, which they want to destroy.“

Trump has cited preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear bomb as a key goal of the war, ⁠along with ending its ability to attack its neighbours and creating conditions for Iranians to topple their leadership. Iran does not have nuclear weapons and denies it wants ​to develop them, but argues it has the right to a domestic ‌nuclear energy capacity.

Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian, in an ‌interview with the CBS show Face the Nation, said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear program and other issues, but would not accept “bullying or ‌coercion”.

“Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that “we’re not supposed to develop nuclear weapons”.

US and Iranian officials spoke separately with mediators on Monday as part of a renewed effort to end the seven-month war, according to officials of both countries.

Anthropic will caution investors that artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” in its IPO prospectus. As Anthropic prepares for an IPO listing, which could value the AI company at a monumental $2tn, it dedicated almost a third of its prospectus to discussing concerns around AI safety. The news comes as OpenAI has halted the release of its next AI model over safety concerns, the Wall Street Journal reports.

Trump will be on the campaign trail this week – hosting rallies in Durant, Oklahoma, on Thursday, Mobile, Alabama, on Friday and Vandalia, Ohio, on Saturday. The first two states are GOP strongholds, and Trump has pushed voters to turn out to the polls and pretend the president was at the top of the ballot this midterm cycle.

Pete Hegseth ordered the defense department to “protect and uphold the reliability of America’s voting mechanisms against external manipulation and disruption from foreign actors” in a 22 September memo. Hegseth’s order comes as concerns about artificial intelligence are on the rise, but also as the Trump administration has spread misinformation about voter fraud. In July, Trump accused China of interfering in the 2020 election, which he lost.

Andrew Bailey said he is stepping down as one of the FBI’s two deputy directors after just over a year in the role – a short tenure that unfolded as he helped oversee several of Trump’s election‑related investigations. Bailey was appointed in August 2025 to serve alongside Dan Bongino at a moment of sharp tension between the FBI and justice department leadership over the handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.

Pope Leo addressed concerns about artificial intelligence and the war in Ukraine during a press conference onboard the papal plane today. Saying that concerns about AI are not “fake news”, the first US pope appeared to criticize Trump, who called concerns about AI a “hoax” during a UN address last week.

title: Nor’easter unearths pieces of 19th-century shipwreck in Massachusetts
excerpt:
Storm seems to have exposed segments of the Warren Sawyer, a wooden vessel that ran aground in 1884

The nor’easter storm that pummeled New England over the weekend looks to have exposed large segment...
body_text:
Storm seems to have exposed segments of the Warren Sawyer, a wooden vessel that ran aground in 1884

The nor’easter storm that pummeled New England over the weekend looks to have exposed large segments of a 19th-century schooner shipwrecked in the so-called graveyard of the Atlantic.

The Warren Sawyer was sailing from New Orleans to Boston carrying cotton and scrap iron when the three-masted wooden vessel ran aground in Nantucket on 22 December 1884. Its captain and crew of seven were rescued and the ship began to break up after several weeks on the shoreline.

Now marine investigators in Massachusetts are looking at splintered timbers fastened together by rusted iron that emerged from the sand during the weekend storm close to where smaller remnants of the lost schooner have been located previously.

The Egan Maritime Institute, a Nantucket-based educational non-profit, by Monday said it was sending staff in the coming days to examine the site and fragments. And the group said it would prepare a report for state archaeologists to help identify the vessel they came from.

The institute, in a statement to the Associated Press, said it was too soon to be sure the newly emerged segments were definitely from the Warren Sawyer.

Nantucket, it said, was one of the “graveyards of the Atlantic” and its “treacherous shoals and inclement weather” contributed to more than 750 wrecks during the 19th century when hundreds of vessels would traverse the island’s waters daily without modern maritime navigation equipment.

But the proximity to the recorded site of the Warren Sawyer’s demise convinced journalist Jason Graziadei, editor of the online news site the Nantucket Current, that it was likely.

Graziadei said he went to the beach on Saturday during the storm with his eight-year-old son after receiving a tip about wreckage on the island’s south shore, and he posted video of what he saw to YouTube.

He said they found the wooden beams on a drive-on beach by the town’s wastewater facility known as the sewer beds after parking and climbing down to the beach because erosion from the storm had formed a steep drop-off.

“Given where it was and where it emerged, it means that everyone who was driving on to the beach this summer was just directly over this,” Graziadei said. “It’s amazing to think from, you know, over 100 years old that it’s still there.”

Records from the Massachusetts Board of Underwater Archaeological Resources show the Warren Sawyer was carrying 1,115 bales of cotton and 28 tons (25.4 metric tonnes) of scrap iron from New Orleans to Boston when it ran aground.

The schooner remained intact on the island’s Miacomet Beach for two weeks, allowing islanders to save 700 bales of cotton using skids and teams of oxen. On 6 January 1885, another storm tore the ship apart, scattering pieces of its hull, remaining cargo and cordage across more than half a mile of beach.

Remnants believed to be from the ship have continued to emerge from the sand. Massachusetts state archaeologists inspected a roughly 42ft (12.8-meter) section of hull exposed on Miacomet Beach in late 2022 and concluded it was probably part of the Warren Sawyer.

A roughly 15ft square section of the lower stern appeared nearby in February 2023, but shifting sands buried it again before state archaeologists could return to document it.

The Egan Institute urged visitors not to disturb the newly exposed wreckage. Massachusetts law prohibits removing, damaging or displacing underwater archaeological resources.

The Associated Press contributed to this report

title: Bail for RAF base suspects suggests no evidence of ‘terror’, say analysts
excerpt:
When a woman driving home to her Gloucestershire village in England in the early hours of Sunday morning found her driveway blocked by three white vans, she immediately called the police.

The call tr...
body_text:
When a woman driving home to her Gloucestershire village in England in the early hours of Sunday morning found her driveway blocked by three white vans, she immediately called the police.

The call triggered a whirlwind of dramatic events; within 15 minutes, armed officers had swooped on the scene, and a major incident was declared at the nearby Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford, a base United States bombers have used to strike Iran.

Some 85 homes were evacuated as a bomb disposal robot picked its way between the vans, and five British men in their 20s were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences.

As army explosives experts examined the vehicles and counterterrorism detectives began questioning the suspects, US President Donald Trump, some 5,800km (3,600 miles) away, was already hailing the arrests.

“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” he told reporters on Sunday.

But Westminster was more cautious, with United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging people “not to speculate”.

Iran’s embassy in London said it “categorically rejects” any link, adding that such speculation would only “fuel Iranophobia propaganda in the UK”.

Then on Monday, all five men were released on bail, leaving Trump “surprised”. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio went further, saying the incident “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor”. He did not name one, though he noted that Iran had “openly threatened to attack American interests globally”.

The swift succession of arrests, claims and subsequent release has left a confused picture, raising questions about whether British authorities were indeed tracking the suspects – as Trump claimed – and whether the case is thinner than Washington suggests, say analysts.

But many analysts Al Jazeera spoke to said that the manner in which the suspects were released suggests that the UK government had little evidence, at least at this point, that the men were plotting a major attack.

Analysts said there were few signs of a sophisticated plot.

“If there had been any trace of explosives found in the vans, or any thoughts that these men were actually terrorists, they would not have been released,” Chris Phillips, a former head of the UK’s National Counter Terrorism Security Office, told Al Jazeera.

“It’s gone from World War III to Four Lions in four hours,” he said, referring to the 2010 British satire about a group of bumbling would-be suicide bombers.

Under the Terrorism Act 2000, police can hold terrorism suspects for up to 14 days without charge, he said, adding that officers who believed they had caught genuine attackers would use that time.

“You keep them, and you go through all their records and all their contacts and what they’ve been doing and what they’ve been talking about,” he said.

Afzal Ashraf, a visiting fellow in international relations and security at Loughborough University and a former senior Royal Air Force officer who served in Iraq, shares the same sentiment.

“If there had been any explosives, big or small, in those vans, then there is no way on Earth that the police would have released these individuals on bail,” he said.

Police have not said whether any explosives were found, with Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor stressing that the men “absolutely remain under investigation”.

One of the vans bore the logo “Fuel 2You”, which BBC Verify found no evidence of being a legitimate company.

Ashraf said many homes in the area, according to the internet, are not connected to the mains gas network and rely on heating oil stored in tanks in their gardens.

He said those tanks have become more valuable as fuel prices have soared during the Iran war.

“When you’ve got several hundred litres in gardens, that’s a bit of a killing for somebody,” he said, stressing that this was “an alternative and probably more plausible explanation” rather than a certainty.

“There’s absolutely nothing else at all, at the moment, suggesting that there is a link to any foreign government,” he added.

Phillips argued that the proximity to the base “may just be a complete fluke”.

“I’m absolutely certain there is intelligence that there are people in the UK that would love to attack,” he said. “But I’m not sure these guys are the ones.”

Anthony Glees, emeritus professor of security and intelligence studies at the University of Buckingham, said the effort that went into the vans pointed to something planned.

“People do steal fuel, and students do do stupid things, but you wouldn’t go to the trouble and expense of taking three white vans to do so,” he said.

Instead, he believes the men were “useful idiots” who had “been hired at some expense” by a foreign state, not to carry out an attack but to stage one to “embarrass the British government”.

If early indications suggest it was not a major terrorist plot, why, then, were Washington’s claims so emphatic?

For Ashraf, the explanation lies in the administration’s handling of the Iran war, which is driven by what he calls “narrative dominance”.

“This particular American administration hasn’t bothered with a strategy, a military strategy, or even a political strategy,” he said. “What it has worked on is a narrative strategy.”

On Trump’s claim that the men had been watched for “a long time”, he suspects a mix-up.

“What possibly has happened is that President Trump has been briefed about several groups, I would guess, that the Americans are tracking, which is normal,” he said.

He added that there may have been “some sort of conflation, which now the president has convinced himself is the same people”.

“Nobody’s going to tell the president he’s got it wrong,” he said.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, a longtime ally of Trump, posted on Monday that “Fairford proves my point on Iran and the IRGC”, referring to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

He had linked the incident to Iranian agents arriving in small boats, before police confirmed all five men were British nationals from London.

For Ashraf, whether the claims hold up may matter little to Trump.

“Even if it’s proven that this is basically a criminal act and nothing to do with terrorism, what he’s successfully done, in the minds of a lot of people, and people like Nigel have amplified it, is just reinforced that association that’s been going on for a long time,” he said.

“That is a hit. That is success as far as they’re concerned.”

Police have not ruled out foreign involvement.

Taylor said investigators were “considering this from every possible angle”. That included the possibility of “activity committed by proxies, or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state”.

Such plots are not new. MI5 Director General Ken McCallum said in October 2025 that the agency had tracked “more than 20 potentially lethal Iran-backed plots” in the UK in the space of a year.

Phillips explained how such recruitment typically works.

“They go onto the dark web, and they post, ‘Would someone like to do a job and make 10,000 pounds?’, as an example,” he said.

The person who carries out the job is often “four or five rungs down the line”, with no direct link to Iran or Russia.

Glees believes Fairford fits that pattern, and puts Iran “in pole position”, but he argued a real attack would have backfired on Tehran.

“If there had been an attack on RAF [Fairford], that would have been an attack on British soil, which would have meant Britain would have to be far more heavily involved in the war against Iran,” he said, adding, “Iran’s got no interest in that.”

Instead, he described it as “a frightener”, designed to embarrass the UK and perhaps make Trump feel the British “couldn’t be counted on”.

Ashraf is sceptical Tehran would take the risk at all.

He said Iran’s messaging has centred on the war being unpopular, even in the US, and that any plot endangering British or American civilians would undermine it.

If Iran had wanted to attack Fairford, he said, it probably would have assembled “a slightly more capable team”.

title: I've battled gangs for decades. Now I'm fighting a threat that's even harder
excerpt:
Fox News host Harris Faulkner has the latest on the winning team approach on 'The Faulkner Focus.'

In my time on the South Side of Chicago, I’ve asked people to look at what we’re losing. I have poin...
body_text:
Fox News host Harris Faulkner has the latest on the winning team approach on 'The Faulkner Focus.'

In my time on the South Side of Chicago, I’ve asked people to look at what we’re losing. I have pointed out the root causes of gun violence, set up programs to counter it, confronted gangsters and brought them to truces, and helped many enter mainstream society as productive citizens. I’ve created after-school programs to counter our failing public schools so that kids won’t give up on themselves. But lately, I’ve been looking at another problem that may just be equally dangerous: the smartphone.

When you look at a smartphone, it doesn’t look like a threat. It looks like a tool for connection and even for opportunity. And for a lot of young people in my neighborhood, it has been exactly that — a way to make music, create an online following and learn about worlds outside of this block. I don’t want to discount what they have done because some have built real careers with nothing but a phone and its many tools. That’s a genuine way out of poverty, and I have no desire to shut that door.

But I can’t ignore the dark side of the phone.

AMERICA MOCKED THE AMISH AND OTHER GROUPS OVER TECHNOLOGY. MAYBE THEY WERE RIGHT

What I feel is that far too few of us acknowledge the full power of the phone. I once watched a documentary that said the power of all the computers needed to put the first man on the moon now existed in our tiny little phones. I don’t know if that’s true, but there is no doubt about the phone’s power. It puts the entire world at a kid’s fingertips.

We have fought many problems in my community, from drugs to gangs. The phone may be even harder.  (iStock)

Where I’ve seen the most devastating impact of the smartphone is in the world of drill rap, which began on O-Block, where my church and community center sit. Drill rap means "kill rap." Some of it is honest storytelling about a life that most of the country has never seen. But some of it has become a weapon.

A phone cannot love a child. It can only hold their eyes through the trickery of the algorithm.

Fights that we used to see on corners have now moved onto livestreams. What happens is that a location tag is then dropped. Sometimes it’s dropped when a drill rap crew chooses to film in the wrong neighborhood as a dare. This dropping of a location is not an accident but a challenge: Come and get us.

INDIANA REPUBLICAN SENATOR MOVES TO BLOCK KIDS FROM ACCESSING PORN ONLINE

So we have kids watching these livestreams, half listening to the rap and half waiting for that burst of gunfire to come. When the latter happens, it is me or one of the nearby pastors who has to host the funeral. We then have to send our violence impact teams to the hospitals and homes of families to prevent retaliatory shootings. All from a livestream playing out on the phones of 10-, 12-, 14- and 17-year-olds.

So the same phone that can build a young artist up — and, man, some of these kids are so talented — that same phone can bring them down. When there is a shooting, the police and prosecutors comb through all these livestreams, and any comments may be treated as confessions. Whatever you think of this legal strategy, some of these kids get locked up.

Yes, put limits on the phone. Yes, tell your child to sit at the table and do homework. Go to church. Look people in the eye when talking. Make them look at reality instead of a screen. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

But the phone isn’t only a problem on the streets. Parents here struggle with the problem of the phone in their homes. I see this in good families that are far removed from the life of gangs or drill rap. Their kids simply cannot put the phone down. Kids can access pornography even before they’ve had a chance to form healthy relationships. Our communities don’t teach courtship much anymore, and for the last several decades, we’ve lived in this hookup culture. So what does a child wired by pornography think when he or she encounters the other sex?

Parents are not always right, but the phone deprives the child and parent of the process of working through that misunderstanding and, in turn, weakens the fabric of their relationship.

Parents often tell me the same thing, and I’m struck by how similar the wording is. It goes something like this: "I don’t know how to take the phone away from my child. It’s like I’m ending their world. I don’t know if I even have the authority to do it. They tell me that if I do, I’m cutting them off. It just becomes an endless battle."

WHAT META'S NEW TEEN RESTRICTIONS MEAN FOR YOUNG PEOPLE

The reality is that the phone often turns into a weapon that the child uses against the authority of the parent. I’ve heard kids tell their parents that they are smarter than them. That’s nothing but an illusion. When a child Googles or uses AI while arguing against a parent, that’s not the same thing as learning or processing the actual argument. That’s using a machine to speak for oneself. And what this ultimately does is stop the child from respecting the authority and knowledge of the parent.

Parents are not always right, but the phone deprives the child and parent of the process of working through that misunderstanding and, in turn, weakens the fabric of their relationship.

That’s the real crisis. Not the technology itself — the erosion of the adult’s ability to set a limit on it.

The solution is not a ban. What I’m calling for is a shift in the culture. We need to return to the basic authority that parents used to take for granted. Yes, take that phone away at night. Yes, put limits on the phone. Yes, tell your child to sit at the table and do homework. Go to church. Look people in the eye when talking. Make them look at reality instead of a screen.

And one thing that we need to do is support these parents. We adults who make up this community must echo this pushback against the phone, so the kids understand that it is not just their parents but the entire community pushing back.

We have fought many problems in my community, from drugs to gangs. The phone may be even harder. But I’ll leave you with this thought: A phone cannot love a child. It can only hold their eyes through the trickery of the algorithm. But somebody has to be there to hold that child and to love that child, and that must be us.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM PASTOR COREY BROOKS

Pastor Corey Brooks, known as the "Rooftop Pastor," is the founder and Senior Pastor of New Beginnings Church of Chicago and the CEO of Project H.O.O.D. (Helping Others Obtain Destiny), the church's local mission. He gained national attention for his 94-day and 343-day rooftop vigils to transform the notorious "O-Block," once known as Chicago's most dangerous block, into #OpportunityBlock. Learn more at ProjectHOOD.org.

title: Spanish government approves measures to ease housing crisis after outcry over eviction
excerpt:
Measures, which need to be approved in Congress, include extending ban on evictions of vulnerable people

Spain’s Socialist Workers’ party-led coalition government has approved a range of measures aim...
body_text:
Measures, which need to be approved in Congress, include extending ban on evictions of vulnerable people

Spain’s Socialist Workers’ party-led coalition government has approved a range of measures aimed at easing the country’s housing crisis, including extending a ban on evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, after a public outcry over the eviction of an 87-year-old disabled woman from her Madrid apartment last week.

Two decrees have been approved by cabinet but will need to be approved in Congress, where the coalition lacks a majority. The government has requested a special parliamentary session on Friday in the hope of getting the decrees passed as soon as possible.

Although the fine print has yet be revealed, the main decree includes: extending restrictions on evictions of vulnerable tenants to 2030; regulating temporary lettings and lettings by room; a ban on so-called vulture funds buying property until 2028, plus a two-year extension on current rental agreements that are due to expire at the end of 2028.

A separate agreement was reached on the automatic renovation of rental agreements.

Hundreds of people remained camped out in ⁠one of Madrid’s main squares on Tuesday to protest against Maricarmen Abascal’s removal from her home on a stretcher last Wednesday. They are demanding legal reforms including a rent freeze and the ⁠automatic renewal of leases without abusive rent hikes.

It is believed that the first decree has the approval of the conservative Catalan and Basque parties, which previously opposed the government’s housing overhauls, but they are likely to vote down the second decree.

Mónica García, the health minister, celebrated the decision, saying: “We’ve achieved something that even a month ago was unthinkable.”

She added: “It’s time to intervene in the speculative housing market and begin to restore the balance between citizens and vulture funds.”

The Tenants’ Union, which has been the driving force behind the demand for changes to the housing law, as well as the occupation of Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol by protesters in recent days, said it needed to read the small print but opposed the policy of dividing the issue into separate decrees.

“It’s a tactic of tearing something into shreds so that all that’s left are scraps,” said Alicia Del Río, a union spokesperson in Madrid. “The union demands the implementation of the Maricarmen decree in its entirety,” she said, referring to a set of changes drawn up by the union. “They have to accept what people are demanding.”

The government has 30 days from the decree’s publication to reach a consensus with allies in congress. Junts, the Catalan pro-independence party that would need to back the decree for it to pass, said on Tuesday it was still far from agreeing to ‌it and wanted protection for small landlords, who make up the vast majority of property owners in Spain.

“Owning two properties isn’t the same as owning entire buildings,” said Míriam Nogueras, Junts’ spokesperson in congress. “But here they’re not making any distinction between the two.”

Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the leader of the conservative People’s party, dismissed the proposals. “The government has created a problem that didn’t exist when it took office,” he said. “A problem that was created over eight years can’t be solved in five minutes.”

Urbagestión, the company whose eviction of Abascal last Wednesday forced the housing crisis to the top of the political agenda, has said Abascal can return to her apartment at a rent that will not exceed 30% of her income. On Tuesday, she accepted the offer and will pay €533 (£457) a month – less than a third of the original demand of €1,650 that had led to her eviction.

Underlining the lack of affordable housing, Ada Colau, a housing activist and a former Barcelona mayor, recently revealed that she has had to move out of her rented apartment after 15 years because it became impossible to pay the rent with a single income since she separated from her husband.

Colau, who renounced most of her mayoral salary during her eight years in office, said the market was geared towards dual incomes, whether couples or people sharing, adding that she had gone to live with a relative.

title: Video shows Florida food truck workers fleeing from ICE during Tallahassee immigration raid
excerpt:
Workers at Chile & Chili’s Tallahassee food truck in Florida scramble to escape Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents during a raid on Sept. 25, 2026.

An Immigration and Customs Enforcemen...
body_text:
Workers at Chile & Chili’s Tallahassee food truck in Florida scramble to escape Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents during a raid on Sept. 25, 2026.

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raid in Tallahassee, Florida prompted mass chaos as security footage showed food truck workers scrambling to flee from federal agents on Friday.

Workers at Chile & Chili’s Taqueria Tallahassee scurried in and out of the food truck’s trailers when federal authorities rolled onto the scene, according to video obtained by Fox News Digital.

Video shows one of the workers, a woman, being apprehended by authorities.

Three of the individuals seen running in the video were Guatemalan nationals who had not yet finalized immigration paperwork, the food truck’s owner reportedly told WCTV.

EXCLUSIVE: LA ICE DIRECTOR REVEALS OFFICERS FOLLOWED HOME, HARASSED AS POLICE FAIL TO HELP IN SANCTUARY CITY

Immigration authorities detain a worker at Chile & Chili’s Tallahassee in Tallahassee, Florida during a raid on Sept. 25, 2026. (Chile & Chili’s Tallahassee via Storyful)

The owner has also reportedly closed the food truck, the owner told WCTV, citing safety concerns and the remainder of the truck’s employees quitting in the wake of the raid.

MINNESOTA'S ANTI-ICE AID FUND BECOMES LATEST CASUALTY OF STATE'S EMBARRASSING FRAUD PROBLEM

Despite the apparent closure, the incident prompted community organizers to plan an anti-ICE rally at the food truck’s Tennessee Street location on Wednesday.
